correctness.rationale: Exact SVD and Gaussian rotational invariance reduce the projected norm to a ratio of two Gaussian quadratic forms; its strict lower-tail event is an absolute Cauchy ratio event; completing the square gives the global supremum attained by r=t/√2. Continuity and monotonicity justify unique inverse calibration. Conditional statement requires fresh independent Gaussian sample. Exact-rational checks, inverse numerical checks and seeded sampling corroborate but do not prove the infinite quantifiers. All boundaries 0<t<1, 0<δ<1, 0<r≤1 and rank two are explicit.

value.rationale: An exact sharp one-sided confidence factor for the actual one-probe projected spectral-norm stopping statistic quantifies how dangerous rank-two residuals can be, including the least-favorable spectrum and the full threshold dependence. It supplies a practical calibration rather than a generic observation that sketches sometimes underestimate. Rank two is the first nontrivial spectral class and one probe the minimal useful indicator; no claim beyond that natural regime is needed.
